channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Sol: near-Astra coding power at a fifth of the price
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI's DevDay keynote brought GPT-6.1 Sol, an upgrade to GPT-6 Sol that nearly matches flagship GPT-6 Astra on agentic coding, computer use, and professional work — at one-fifth of Astra's token price.

item.title: Stop writing your own agent loop: a hands-on tutorial for OpenAI's Agents API
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: OpenAI’s DevDay put a managed agent harness behind a single API call. Build a long-running, tool-using agent on the Agents API — sessions, sandboxes, MCP tools, subagents, and cleanup — with every line verified against the official docs.

item.title: OpenAI’s DevDay got an AI-made Sam Altman × Dario Amodei parody — and Reddit identified the tool behind it
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: On OpenAI’s DevDay, the most-shared post on r/OpenAI wasn’t an announcement — it was a joke: an AI-generated music-video parody starring Sam Altman and Dario Amodei. The comments did what they do best, and named the tool that made it.

item.title: Impeccable: teach your AI coding agent to design like a design director — hands-on with the 72K-star skill
item.dc:creator: Elena Vasquez
item.description: Impeccable, Paul Bakaus’s 72K-star design skill for AI coding agents, pairs 24 named design commands with 61 deterministic detector rules that run with no LLM and no API key. I scanned a deliberate AI-slop page hands-on — 12 findings down to zero — and documented every command.

item.title: Hands-on with NVIDIA Model Optimizer: quantize once, export anywhere
item.dc:creator: Elena Vasquez
item.description: NVIDIA's Model Optimizer gained ~900 GitHub stars in four days: one Python API for quantization, pruning, distillation, and speculative decoding, plus a unified export to TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, and SGLang. I ran INT8 weight-only quantization end-to-end on a CPU-only VM — 6.5 seconds, no quality loss, one-third smaller checkpoint — and documented the INT4 AWQ attempt the sandbox OOM-killed.

item.title: Flatkey raises $10M for one API key that reaches 100+ models and 1,000 tools — most of them below list price
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: San Jose's Flatkey announced a $10M Series A Tuesday after passing 10,000 developers in two months, pitching one key, one balance, and one invoice for 100+ official models and 1,000+ AI tools — at 60 to 90% of the labs' list prices.

item.title: Reco raises $55M to secure the AI agents your company doesn't know it has — AT&T Ventures leads
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: AI security startup Reco announced Tuesday it has raised $55 million in additional strategic funding led by AT&T Ventures, bringing its total raised to $140 million. The company maps every AI agent operating inside a customer’s business — including the ones nobody authorized.

item.title: Cribl launches StreamAI: an AI gateway with a model router that cuts the token bill — free inference when the router picks
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Cribl's new StreamAI gateway routes each prompt to the cheapest model that gets the job done — and inference is free when the router picks the model. Its SecIT Bench found just a 17% accuracy spread but a 20x cost spread across 20 AI models.

item.title: Anthropic's confidential IPO prospectus reveals up to $84.5B in SpaceX compute deals through 2029
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Reuters' review of Anthropic's confidential IPO prospectus surfaces compute agreements with SpaceX worth up to $84.5 billion through 2029 — nearly double earlier disclosures — inside a $518 billion decade-long infrastructure buildout.

item.title: PageIndex: vectorless, reasoning-based RAG you can run on your own models — hands-on
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: PageIndex hit 37,000 GitHub stars by throwing away the vector database: it indexes PDFs as hierarchical trees and sends an agent to walk them. I ran the whole loop locally with my own model — here is the full hands-on tutorial.

item.title: Trump launches America.gov: an AI-powered front door for every federal service
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: The federal government now has one official AI chatbot for everything from passports to Medicare — powered by Google’s Gemini and Elon Musk’s Grok, and backed by an executive order. Here’s what launched, what it changes, and what to watch.

item.title: Microsoft Research unveils Quine: a world model of biology that already picks cancer drugs
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Microsoft Research introduced Quine, a multimodal world model of biology with a scientist-in-the-loop harness. With the Broad Institute, it ranked thousands of compounds for pancreatic tumor cell-state shifts — top picks validated in the wet lab. Quine Fellows applications open today.

item.title: OpenAI launches $500/month Pro 500 tier with Astra Ultrafast at DevDay as the $200 Pro plan gets halved
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: OpenAI used DevDay to redraw its ChatGPT Pro ladder: a new $500/mo Pro 500 tier with an Ultrafast mode for Codex and Work, while the reopened $200 Pro 200 ships with half the usage it used to have. Existing subscribers keep their current limits until October 29 — and they are not happy.

item.title: Give your AI agent a real memory: hands-on with Hindsight, the local-first memory layer
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Hindsight (42k GitHub stars) gives AI agents persistent memory: retain facts, recall them with hybrid search, and reflect over them agentically — all running locally on Ollama. We verified every step end-to-end on a 2-core CPU box.

item.title: Ship your own AI news desk in an afternoon: a hands-on guide to AIHOT
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Clone it, boot it with four commands, and you have a self-running news desk: AIHOT collects from six source types, double-scores every item with an LLM, clusters reports into events, ranks by heat, and publishes a daily briefing at 08:00.

item.title: OpenAI launches Dots — always-on AI agents with their own cloud computer — at DevDay 2026
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI's DevDay keynote shipped 20+ products: Dots, always-on AI agents powered by GPT-6 Astra with their own cloud computer; a shared ChatGPT Space workspace; and GPT-6.1 Sol at a fifth of Astra's token prices.

item.title: Thought Machine and AWS will turn banks' COBOL into Python in days — AI agents extract the intent, humans sign off
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Thought Machine and AWS today launched a joint AI-powered migration pipeline that turns millions of lines of COBOL into tested Python financial products in a live sandbox — compressing multi-year core banking migrations into days, with a human sign-off gate before anything ships.

item.title: Stop paying flagship prices for easy questions: build an LLM cascade router that escalates only when it matters
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Your API bill is dominated by easy questions answered by your most expensive model. Build a cascade router that tries the cheap model first and escalates only when confidence is low — pricing, backends, scorers, and thresholds, measured end-to-end.

item.title: OpenAI's annualized revenue run rate nears $70 billion as enterprise sales double
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: OpenAI's annualized revenue run rate is nearing $70 billion — up more than 70% since the start of Q3, with enterprise sales more than doubling since July, according to sources who spoke to Axios.

item.title: Trump gathers AI's biggest CEOs at the White House as the safety debate reaches his table
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Six AI chiefs — Zuckerberg, Amodei, Brockman, Pichai, Karp and Huang — sit down with Trump and Speaker Johnson today as Washington wrestles with a question that suddenly has teeth: how much oversight can AI take without losing the race to China.

item.title: Muse goes to work: Meta wires its AI agent into QuickBooks, Stripe, Shopify and 12 more business tools
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Meta's Muse AI agent now connects to 15 third-party business apps plus Facebook and Instagram business accounts, so owners can hand it goals like finding new customers. Publishing, messaging, and spending still need approval.

item.title: HSBC launches HSBCnio: your bank account plugs into your AI tools via MCP
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: HSBC's new HSBCnio platform embeds transaction banking into the systems clients already use — and lets their own AI tools query account data through HSBC's Model Context Protocol.

item.title: Stop feeding your agent the whole repo: a hands-on tutorial for code-review-graph
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: code-review-graph (26,500+ stars, 6,400 added in a single week) builds a persistent local map of your codebase — functions, callers, tests, blast radius — and serves it to any AI coding agent over MCP. Install, build, wire it up, and run a real change-impact review — every command verified.

item.title: Claude goes down: Anthropic confirms partial outage across claude.ai, Claude Code, and the API
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Anthropic confirmed a partial outage on September 29 affecting Claude, Claude Code, Claude Cowork, the API, and the Console. Reports spiked just before 10:30am ET; a mitigation landed within about 40 minutes.

item.title: Kyunghyun Cho launches Ortet: a $500M frontier AI lab for a patient-centered health model
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Attention co-inventor Kyunghyun Cho has a new lab. Ortet, backed by a $500 million commitment from Thoreau, will build a patient-centered foundation model that learns across biology, clinical care, operations, and finance — the frontier-lab playbook, pointed at health.
